q: Sound is a form of _____ that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium.
e: Sound is a form of energy that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium. Energy here means the capacity to do work. Matter: anything that has mass and occupies space.

q: Sound wave is produced by a _____ object placed in a medium.
e: Sound wave is produced by a vibrating object placed in a medium. The physics in this sentence is built around vibrating.

q: Sound wave propagates as a series of compression and _____ like longitudinal waves.
e: Sound wave propagates as a series of compression and rarefaction like longitudinal waves. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound. Reflection: light bouncing back from a surface.

q: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a medium to propagate and cannot travel through _____.
e: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a medium to propagate and cannot travel through vacuum. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: The compression region in a sound wave has _____ pressure.
e: The compression region in a sound wave has higher pressure. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: When the vibrating object moves back, the molecules are spread out and _____ is created.
e: When the vibrating object moves back, the molecules are spread out and rarefaction is created. The physics in this sentence is built around rarefaction.

q: Sound energy is transferred through the medium by successive pressure changes without moving the _____ as a whole.
e: Sound energy is transferred through the medium by successive pressure changes without moving the medium as a whole. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: When sound waves enter the ear, they strike the _____ and make it vibrate.
e: When sound waves enter the ear, they strike the ear drum and make it vibrate. The physics in this sentence is built around ear drum.

q: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than 20 Hz and lower than _____ Hz.
e: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than 20 Hz and lower than 20 000 Hz. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The interval of frequency from 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz is called the _____ range.
e: The interval of frequency from 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz is called the audible range. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: Sound waves with frequencies greater than 20 000 Hz are called _____.
e: Sound waves with frequencies greater than 20 000 Hz are called ultrasounds. Ultrasounds names sound waves with frequencies greater than 20 000 Hz.

q: Sound waves with frequencies under 20 Hz are called _____.
e: Sound waves with frequencies under 20 Hz are called infrasound. Infrasound names sound waves with frequencies under 20 Hz.

q: Elephants can communicate with _____.
e: Elephants can communicate with infrasound. The physics in this sentence is built around infrasound.

q: Dogs, bats, and dolphins can hear and communicate with _____.
e: Dogs, bats, and dolphins can hear and communicate with ultrasound. The physics in this sentence is built around ultrasound.

q: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the _____ of the medium.
e: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the density of the medium. Density here means mass per unit volume.

q: The denser the medium is, the _____ the speed of sound because the particles are tightly bound together.
e: The denser the medium is, the greater the speed of sound because the particles are tightly bound together. The physics in this sentence is built around greater.

q: At 0°C, the speed of sound in air is _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: At 0°C, the speed of sound in air is 332 $\text{m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around 332.

q: Whenever the air temperature increases by 1°C, the speed of sound will increase by _____ %.
e: Whenever the air temperature increases by 1°C, the speed of sound will increase by 0.2 %. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$ with a temperature rise of one degree.
e: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by 0.6 $\text{m s}^{-1}$ with a temperature rise of one degree. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The speed of sound in air can be expressed by the formula $v = 332 \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}}$, where $T$ is given in _____.
e: The speed of sound in air can be expressed by the formula $v = 332 \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}}$, where $T$ is given in K. The physics in this sentence is built around K.

q: The approximate relation for the speed of sound in air with temperature $T$ in Kelvin is $v = $ _____.
e: The approximate relation for the speed of sound in air with temperature $T$ in Kelvin is $v = $ $332 + 0.6(T - 273)$. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in pure water at 0°C is _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in pure water at 0°C is 1404 $\text{m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around 1404.

q: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in copper at 20°C is _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in copper at 20°C is 3560 $\text{m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around 3560.
